subject: Discovery Recap: Private VPC & On-Prem Requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acmehealth.com>, Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Private VPC & On-Prem Requirements

Hi Alice / Ben — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned. Let me know if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points & goals
- Regulatory: clinical workloads need to remain HIPAA-compliant (PHI). Primary concern: no egress of PHI to shared multi-tenant endpoints.
- Network constraints: for clinical inference you require an air-gapped or strictly customer-managed VPC/on-prem deployment with no outbound internet from inference nodes.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) mandatory for PHI cases; need support for on-prem HSM (KMIP) and cloud KMS (AWS/Azure).
- Audit & controls: must capture detailed audit logs, token-level usage, and retain them for 7 years (compliance requirement).

Current stack (as discussed)
- Primary compute: on-prem Kubernetes clusters (RHEL) in their clinical data center for PHI workloads.
- Identity: Okta SSO, SCIM provisioning.
- Storage: encrypted NFS for model/artifact storage.

Success criteria for a PoC
- No PHI leaves customer-controlled network during inference for clinical workloads.
- Demonstrate KMS/HSM integration with customer-managed keys.
- End-to-end audit trail for 1-week synthetic workload.
- Latency & throughput targets met for clinical inference SLA (p95 < 300ms for 1k reqs/day profile).

Constraints & notes
- We discussed a hybrid approach: clinical inference on air-gapped/on-prem; non-PHI workloads could run in a dedicated VPC (hosted).
- Network team will need a list of outbound ports/ips for the control plane if you allow limited egress.

Next steps
1) ACME: share internal network diagram and any SOC/Security questionnaire items (you mentioned the network diagram in the call).
2) Redwood: we'll share a high-level Private/VPC architecture doc and our KMS/HSM integration matrix (attached).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra + security teams (suggested windows Mar 17-19).
4) Agree on PoC scope and timeline (target: 2-3 week lab PoC starting week of Mar 29).

Attachments: Redwood_Private_VPC_Highlevel.pdf (overview), link to architecture doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cRedwoodPrivateOverview

Thanks — I'll follow up here once I have the internal notes captured and a proposed calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Alice Tan <alice.tan@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Lowe <ben.lowe@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:01:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Private VPC & On-Prem Requirements

Thanks Marissa — this looks accurate and helpful. A few clarifications / asks from our side:

- The air-gap requirement applies only to "clinical inference" (PHI). For analytics and non-PHI workloads we are open to a dedicated VPC in the cloud.
- We will send over an updated network diagram (ACME_network_diagram_v2.pdf) — it includes the demarcation points for clinical systems.
- Can Redwood provide a quick matrix for KMS/HSM support? Specifically we need to confirm support for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault and on-prem HSMs via KMIP. Also need an initial estimate on licensing/PoC costs for the PoC scope you proposed.

Would like the technical deep-dive with your infra/security present. Preferred dates are Mar 17 (afternoon) or Mar 18 (morning).

Appreciate the quick recap — attaching the network diagram.

Best,
Alice Tan
Head of Clinical Informatics, Acme Health
alice.tan@acmehealth.com
+1 (617) 555-8873

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Private VPC & On-Prem Requirements

Thanks Alice — great context and the diagram is helpful. Quick answers and next actions: 

- KMS/HSM support: Redwood supports AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault natively for dedicated/cloud deployments. For on-prem HSM we integrate via KMIP-compatible connectors (we have customers using Thales and Utimaco setups). I’ll share our KMS/HSM matrix as an attachment.
- Costs / PoC: I’ll put together a short estimate for a 2-3 week PoC (license + engineering time + any infra connectors). Expect that in the next 48 hours.
- Tech deep-dive: proposing Mar 17, 10:00–11:30 PT — does that work for your security/infra teams? If not we can do Mar 18 morning.

Deliverables from Redwood before the deep-dive:
- SOC 2 Type II summary and relevant audit evidence links
- KMS/HSM integration matrix (attached: redwood_infra_kms_matrix.csv)
- Initial PoC runbook/acceptance criteria draft

I’ve attached the KMS matrix and will follow up with the PoC estimate and a calendar invite for Mar 17 (tentative).

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood_infra_kms_matrix.csv
